items.title: Steve Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: He was doing a performance somewhere and his usual pianist, who was Teddy Wilson, the great black pianist, was not available that week... So that's how Benny was about names.

ctx.x: I understand Sol Yaged came out and gave you some —

Yeah. As soon as I agreed to do the movie then of course the question was even though I was a musician I knew nothing about the clarinet, so we had to hire somebody to teach me, and somebody knew about Sol, our mutual friend Bobby Rosengarden once said something hysterically funny, he described Sol Yaged as quote the Jewish Benny Goodman. For you young people, Benny himself is Jewish. But anyway Sol was the perfect choice, and a very easy guy to work with, so he gave me several weeks of just basic lessons, you…

Benny Goodman lived in a fog. He was Mr. Absent Minded and often didn’t know what he was doing. He’d walk on stage with his fly open and stuff. And through accident, he was just a careless man and didn’t think much about the world. He was just the greatest clarinet player of them all. So just after the movie, NBC and Universal Studios got together to do a little promotion going in both directions, so that meant booking Benny on our show, which was on the air Sunday nights at NBC at the time. So Benny himself…

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: That's right, Steve Allen played the role of Benny Goodman, and Sol coached Steve Allen on synchronizing the camera shots with the sound track.

ctx.x: We were talking about when you went out to California to do the picture, The Benny Goodman Story. Now there should be some interesting things to tell about that. Let's see, Sol Yaged was teaching somebody to play Benny ...

That's right, Steve Allen played the role of Benny Goodman, and Sol coached Steve Allen on synchronizing the camera shots with the sound track. See, they recorded the whole sound track -- the music was all recorded first, and then the camera work was done later with the sound track being blasted over loud speakers for the musicians to hear and memorize the improvisations as they go over it again and again, until they finally got a pretty good synchronization of sound and sight.

So it was recorded first, because Goodman recorded all the clarinet on the sound track, but Steve Allen was photographed doing it all, and Sol was his coach and taught him how to hold the clarinet and to make it appear plausible that he was actually playing the clarinet when he wasn't.
